# Items and equipment reference

The equipment component, world pickups, the item, rarity, tag and set assets, and the requirement and set-bonus data they carry. For how to use it, see [Items and equipment](../modules/items.md).

## VtUnitEquipment

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Items → VtUnitEquipment**. Adds [VtUnitModifiers](units.md#vtunitmodifiers), [VtUnitTraits](units.md#vtunittraits) automatically.

Per-unit equipment state — owns the slot map (which item is in which slot) and is the orchestrator for the equip / unequip flow. Drives modifier / attribute-grant / trait-override pushes through the unit's `VtUnitModifiers` + `VtUnitTraits` siblings under the source id `"equipment_<slot>"`.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two Hand Rule (`twoHandRule`) | [VtTwoHandRule](#vttwohandrule) | `OffHandComesOff` | What happens to the off-hand item when a two-handed item goes into the main hand. Off Hand Comes Off puts it in the bag; Off Hand Suspended keeps it worn without its bonuses until the two-hander leaves; Off Hand Blocks Two Hander refuses the two-hander while an off-hand item is worn. Read when gear goes on or comes off; a change during play applies from the next one. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `IReadOnlyDictionary<VtEquipmentSlot, VtItemDefinition> Equipped { get; }` | Read-only view of the slot map. Iterate to render an inventory panel or compute set-piece totals. |
| `IReadOnlyList<VtActiveSet> ActiveSets { get; }` | Snapshot of all sets with at least one piece equipped. Each entry reports the set definition, equipped piece count, and the highest currently active tier index (or -1 when no tier threshold is met). Allocates a fresh list each call — UI panels typically call this on `OnSetTierChanged`, not every frame. |
| `bool IsHeldFromInventory { get; }` | True while the main hand shows the selected slot of a `VtUnitHeldSlot` rather than an item worn the usual way. The item then stays in the bag; saves do not list it as worn. |
| `event Action<VtEquipmentSlot, VtItemDefinition> OnEquipped` | Fired after an item is successfully equipped (incl. via the replication entry point). Args: (slot, item). |
| `event Action<VtEquipmentSlot, VtItemDefinition> OnUnequipped` | Fired after an item is successfully unequipped. Args: (slot, item). |
| `event Action<VtEquipmentSlot, int, int> OnDurabilityChanged` | Fired after durability changes on an equipped slot. Args: (slot, current, max), where max is `GetMaxDurability`, which includes copies combined into the item. Fires on equip (initial fill), `ApplyWear`, `RepairItem`, `RepairAll` and when a copy combines into the worn item. Does not fire when an indestructible item is equipped / unequipped. |
| `event Action<VtEquipmentSlot, VtItemDefinition> OnItemBroken` | Fired exactly once per slot when an item's durability hits zero. Args: (slot, item). Subscribers can choose whether to repair, replace, or cosmetically handle the broken state. Auto-unequip (when `VtItemDefinition.autoUnequipOnBreak` is true) fires *after* this event. A main-hand item held from a `VtUnitHeldSlot` is taken from its slot by the held slot's own handler, so a handler that runs after it may find the main hand already empty. |
| `event Action<VtItemSetDefinition, int, int> OnSetTierChanged` | Fired when a set's *top* active tier index changes — activated, deactivated, or upgraded / downgraded between tiers. Args: (set, oldTopTierIndex, newTopTierIndex). `-1` means "no tier active". Subscribers update set-bonus UI panels off this; the source-bag mutations have already happened by the time this fires. |
| `event Action<VtEquipmentSlot, bool> OnSlotSuspended` | Fired when a worn item is suspended or active again, such as the off-hand item while a two-handed item is held under `VtTwoHandRule.OffHandSuspended`. Args: (slot, suspended). Visuals hide it. |
| `bool IsSuspended(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | True when the item in `slot` is worn but gives nothing right now. Suspended items do not count toward sets. |
| `VtItemDefinition GetEquipped(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | Item currently in the given slot, or null if the slot is empty. |
| `bool IsEquipped(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | True if any item occupies the given slot. |
| `bool IsEquipped(VtItemDefinition item, VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | True if this specific item is in the given slot. |
| `int GetDurability(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | Current durability of the item in the given slot. Returns 0 if the slot is empty or the equipped item is indestructible. |
| `int GetMaxDurability(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | Maximum durability of the item in the given slot: its authored `VtItemDefinition.maxDurability` plus `GetExtraDurability`. Returns 0 if the slot is empty or the item is indestructible (`maxDurability == 0`). |
| `int GetExtraDurability(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | Durability that copies combined into the item in `slot` added (`VtDurabilityMode.Uses`). 0 for a single copy, an empty slot and every other item. |
| `VtInventoryEntry GetWornEntry(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | The item in `slot` as a bag entry would hold it, with its wear and extra durability. An empty slot gives an entry without an item. |
| `int GetWear(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | Durability the item in `slot` has lost: max minus current. 0 for empty slots and items that do not wear out. Taking the item off into the bag keeps this wear on the bag entry. |
| `float GetDurabilityFraction(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | Durability as a 0..1 fraction. Returns 1f for empty slots and indestructible items (so a UI bar can render "full / N/A" uniformly). |
| `int GetSetPieceCount(VtItemSetDefinition set)` | Number of equipped members of the given set (0 when none). Cheap — reads from a cached map, doesn't walk slots. |
| `int GetActiveTierIndex(VtItemSetDefinition set)` | Highest active tier index (into `VtItemSetDefinition.tiers`) for the given set, or `-1` if no tier is currently active. |
| `bool CanEquip(VtItemDefinition item, VtEquipmentSlot slot, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Pure query — returns whether the item *could* be equipped right now, ignoring slot occupancy (useful for tooltip "you can equip this" gating). `TryEquip` performs occupancy checks and the actual mutation. |
| `bool CanEquip(VtItemDefinition item, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Convenience overload that uses the item's authored slot. |
| `bool TryEquip(VtItemDefinition item, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Equip the item into its authored slot, picking a family member when applicable (first empty Ring1 / Ring2; first empty Trinket1 / Trinket2; falls back to replacing the first member if both full). |
| `bool TryEquip(VtItemDefinition item, VtEquipmentSlot slot, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Equip the item into the explicit slot. The slot must match the item's authored slot (or be in the same Ring / Trinket family). |
| `bool TryEquipFromInventory(VtItemDefinition item, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Wear `item` from the unit's `VtUnitInventory`: one is taken out of the bag and whatever it replaces goes back in. Durability carries both ways: the copy put on keeps the wear its bag entry had (the newest copy when several differ), and the replaced items keep theirs. Refused with `VtEquipFailureReason.InventoryFull` when the replaced items would not fit, and with `VtEquipFailureReason.WouldOverflowInventory` when the swap lowers the bag's capacity below what it holds. On a predicting client the request is forwarded and this returns false with `VtEquipFailureReason.AuthorityNotLocal`. |
| `bool TryEquipFromInventory(VtItemDefinition item, VtEquipmentSlot slot, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Like `TryEquipFromInventory`, into `slot`, such as the second ring slot. `VtEquipmentSlot.None` picks the item's own slot. |
| `bool TryUnequipToInventory(VtEquipmentSlot slot, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Take off the item in `slot` and put it in the unit's `VtUnitInventory`. Refused with `VtEquipFailureReason.InventoryFull` when the bag has no room, and with `VtEquipFailureReason.WouldOverflowInventory` when the item adds to the bag's capacity and the bag would no longer hold what it holds. Forwarded like `TryEquipFromInventory`. |
| `bool Unequip(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | Unequip the item in the given slot. Returns true if a slot was emptied, false if the slot was already empty, authority refused, or the item adds to the bag's capacity and the bag would no longer hold what it holds. |
| `bool TryEquipFromSlot(VtInventorySlotRef from, VtEquipmentSlot slot, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Wear the item in bag slot `from` in `slot` (`VtEquipmentSlot.None` picks the item's own slot). That exact copy goes on, with its wear, and what it replaces goes back into `from` when that slot takes it, else into the bag. When the slot already wears a copy of the same `VtDurabilityMode.Uses` item, the bag copy combines into the worn one instead: its durability adds to the worn item and the bag slot empties, without taking the worn item off. Refused like `TryEquipFromInventory`. On a predicting client the request is sent and this returns false with `VtEquipFailureReason.AuthorityNotLocal`. |
| `bool TryUnequipToSlot(VtEquipmentSlot slot, VtInventorySlotRef to, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Take off the item in `slot` into bag slot `to`. When `to` holds an item that can be worn in `slot`, the two swap; when it holds a copy of the same `VtDurabilityMode.Uses` item, the worn copy comes off and combines into it. Refused with `VtEquipFailureReason.TargetSlotRefused` when `to` holds something else, is shut or its rules refuse the item, and otherwise like `TryUnequipToInventory`. On a predicting client the request is sent. |
| `bool TryMoveWorn(VtEquipmentSlot from, VtEquipmentSlot to, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Move a worn item to another equipment slot it fits, such as a ring from the first ring slot to the second, swapping with what is there. Durability moves with each item. On a predicting client the request is sent. |
| `VtEquipmentSlot FreeSlotFor(VtItemDefinition item)` | The slot `item` would go into without anything coming off it (the first free ring or trinket slot of a pair), or `VtEquipmentSlot.None` when that slot is taken or the item is not worn. |
| `bool PassesTwoHandRule(VtItemDefinition item, VtEquipmentSlot slot, out VtEquipFailureReason reason)` | Whether `twoHandRule` lets `item` go into `slot` with what is worn now: an off-hand item while a two-hander is held, or a two-hander while an off-hand item is worn. A drag view asks this with `CanEquip`. |
| `bool ApplyWear(VtEquipmentSlot slot, int amount)` | Reduce the durability of the item in the given slot by `amount`. Authority-gated. Indestructible items (`maxDurability == 0`) and empty slots are no-ops. When durability hits zero, `OnItemBroken` fires; if the item's `VtItemDefinition.autoUnequipOnBreak` is true, the slot is also cleared (firing `OnUnequipped`). |
| `void RepairItem(VtEquipmentSlot slot, int amount)` | Restore `amount` durability on the slot, clamped to `VtItemDefinition.maxDurability`. Authority-gated. No-op on empty slots, indestructible items and `VtDurabilityMode.Uses` items, whose uses are spent, not damaged. |
| `void RepairAll()` | Restore every equipped slot's durability to the item's authored max. Authority-gated. Indestructible and `VtDurabilityMode.Uses` items unaffected. Common pattern: "visit the blacksmith → all gear repaired." |
| `void ApplyEquippedFromNet(VtEquipmentSlot slot, VtItemDefinition item)` | Net-replication entry point: mirror an authoritative equip on a replica. Bypasses the authority gate and the requirement / two-hand checks (the authority already validated them); pushes the modifier / attribute / trait sources locally so derived state stays consistent with the host. Durability seeds to the item's authored max — call the overload to mirror a partial-wear snapshot. |
| `void ApplyEquippedFromNet(VtEquipmentSlot slot, VtItemDefinition item, int currentDurability)` | Net-replication entry point with a durability snapshot — used when the authoritative side has already taken wear and the replica must mirror the current value (e.g. late-join). `currentDurability` is clamped to `[0, item.maxDurability]`; ignored for indestructible items. |
| `void ApplyEquippedFromNet(VtEquipmentSlot slot, VtItemDefinition item, int currentDurability, int extraDurability)` | Like `ApplyEquippedFromNet`, for an item that copies were combined into: `extraDurability` is `GetExtraDurability` on the authority, and `currentDurability` is clamped to the item's maximum with it. |
| `void ApplyUnequippedFromNet(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | Net-replication entry point: mirror an authoritative unequip. |
| `static string SetSourceIdFor(VtItemSetDefinition set, int requiredPieces)` | Source id contract for set-tier rows: `"set_<setId>_<tier>pc"`. Public so consumer net-replication code can mirror or filter on it. |
| `static string SourceIdFor(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | Source id for a given slot — convention is `"equipment_<slot>"`. |
| `static bool SlotsMatch(VtEquipmentSlot itemSlot, VtEquipmentSlot candidate)` | True if the candidate slot is acceptable for an item authored to a specific slot — exact match, or both members of the same family (Ring1/Ring2, Trinket1/Trinket2). |

## VtUnitEquipmentVisuals

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Items → VtUnitEquipmentVisuals**.

Bridges `VtUnitEquipment` events to per-rig visual prefab spawn / despawn. Holds the slot → attach-point Transform mapping that describes where on the wearer's model each equipped item should appear (right_hand bone for MainHand, head bone for Head, etc.).

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attach Points (`attachPoints`) | [VtUnitEquipmentVisuals.SlotAttachPoint](#vtunitequipmentvisualsslotattachpoint)[] | Empty | Slot → bone/transform map for this rig. Author one entry per slot the character should display equipped visuals for. Slots not in this list silently skip visual spawning — useful for rigs that don't have a corresponding bone (a wolf has no Ring1 finger). |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `void Initialize()` | Cache the sibling `VtUnitEquipment`, subscribe to its events, and re-spawn visuals for items already equipped. Idempotent — safe to call any number of times; call it right after adding the component from code. |

## VtWorldItem

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Items → VtWorldItem**.

World-space representation of a pickable `VtItemDefinition` — the dropped sword on the ground, the loot bag the boss left behind, the chest of potions the player walks past. Implements `IVtPickable` so `VtTopDownClickInput` can route right-click → walk-to → auto-pickup uniformly with attackables.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Item (`item`) | [VtItemDefinition](#vtitemdefinition) | None |  | Item definition this world pickup represents. Pickup pushes it into the picker's VtUnitInventory. |
| Count (`count`) | `int` | 1 | ≥ 1 | How many copies are added to the picker's inventory on pickup. Stackable items merge into a single entry. |
| Wear (`wear`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Wear the copies already took, such as a worn axe someone dropped. Picked-up copies keep it. |
| Extra Durability (`extraDurability`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Durability added by copies combined into this one (items with Durability Mode Uses). 0 for a single copy. |
| Pickup Radius (`pickupRadius`) | `float` | 1.5 | ≥ 0 | Distance (world units) within which the picker can grab this item. The walk-to-pickup flow stops here. |
| Destroy On Pickup (`destroyOnPickup`) | `bool` | On |  | Destroy this GameObject after a successful pickup. Disable for chests / containers that should stay in the scene. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUnit ReservedFor { get; }` | The killer whose party may pick this up while reserved, or null. |
| `float ReserveRemaining { get; }` | Seconds left on the reservation; 0 when anyone may pick it up. |
| `event Action<VtUnit> OnPickedUp` | Fired after a successful pickup, before the GameObject is destroyed (if `destroyOnPickup` is true). Subscribers can play VFX, broadcast quest progress, etc. |
| `event Action<VtUnit, int> OnPartlyPickedUp` | Fired when the picker's inventory took only part of the stack. Args: (picker, how many it took). The rest stays on the ground in `count`. |
| `void Reserve(VtUnit owner, float seconds)` | Let only `owner` and its party pick this up for `seconds`. The loot dropper calls this for party kills. |
| `bool IsReservedAgainst(VtUnit picker)` | True when a reservation keeps `picker` from taking this now. |
| `void Tick(float deltaTime)` | Count the reservation down. |

## VtItemDefinition

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Items → Item Definition**.

Designer-authored item — equippable gear, consumable, or quest token. Items are pure data: the runtime `VtUnitEquipment` reads the slot, modifiers, attribute grants, and trait overrides from this asset and pushes them as a single source-bag row keyed `"equipment_<slot>"`.

### Inspector fields

#### Identity

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty |  | Stable string identifier for DB / network payloads. Convention: lowercase dotted, e.g. 'item.sword_of_strength', 'item.health_potion'. Unique across all VtItemDefinition assets. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty |  | UI display name shown to players. Falls back to asset name if empty. |
| Description (`description`) | `string` | Empty |  | Tooltip / lore description shown in-inventory and on hover. |
| Icon (`icon`) | `Sprite` | None |  | Icon shown in inventory grids and tooltips. Optional — consumer UI may fall back to a placeholder. |
| Icon Id (`iconId`) | `string` | Empty |  | Name of an icon from the package's icon set (VtIcons), used when Icon is empty. Optional. |
| Equipped Visual Prefab (`equippedVisualPrefab`) | `GameObject` | None |  | Optional prefab spawned on the wearer's model when this item is equipped (weapon mesh, helmet visual, glow VFX). Parented under the matching attach-point Transform on the wearer's VtUnitEquipmentVisuals. Despawned automatically on unequip. Null = no visual (most items — potions, rings, tokens, anything that doesn't need a 3D representation on the body). |
| World Item Prefab (`worldItemPrefab`) | `GameObject` | None |  | Prefab spawned when a unit drops this item from its bag. Must hold a VtWorldItem. Empty uses the Default World Item Prefab on VtTuning. |
| Rarity (`rarity`) | [VtItemRarityDefinition](#vtitemraritydefinition) | None |  | Rarity tier — drives UI tinting, sort order, and any consumer-side gating. Pick from the five shipped Rarities (Common / Uncommon / Rare / Epic / Legendary) or any custom VtItemRarityDefinition you've authored. Null = no rarity classification. |
| Tags (`tags`) | [VtItemTagDefinition](#vtitemtagdefinition)[] | Empty |  | Categorical labels for this item — drag in VtItemTagDefinition assets (Cursed.asset, Soulbound.asset, …). Consumers: loot filters, trade restrictions, dismantle UI, sort views. Query at runtime via item.HasTag(tagAsset). Host-game-specific — author your tag assets in Assets/Data/Items/Tags/. |
| Set (`set`) | [VtItemSetDefinition](#vtitemsetdefinition) | None |  | Optional item set this item belongs to. When the wearer has multiple members equipped, the set's tier bonuses activate. Null = solo item. |

#### Slot

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slot (`slot`) | [VtEquipmentSlot](#vtequipmentslot) | `None` |  | Which slot the item occupies when equipped. None = inventory-only / non-equippable (potions, materials, quest items). Ring1 / Ring2 and Trinket1 / Trinket2 are families; the no-slot equip overload picks the first empty member. |
| Requires Two Hands (`requiresTwoHands`) | `bool` | Off |  | Two-handed weapon — when equipped to MainHand, the OffHand slot is auto-unequipped and any subsequent attempt to equip into OffHand is blocked until this 2H is removed. Only meaningful for slot == MainHand items. |

#### Stacking (inventory)

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Is Stackable (`isStackable`) | `bool` | Off |  | Stackable items merge into a single inventory entry up to maxStackSize. Typical for consumables (potions, scrolls), materials, ammo. Equipment items are usually unique. |
| Max Stack Size (`maxStackSize`) | `int` | 1 | ≥ 1 | Maximum stack size. Ignored when isStackable is false. 0 / 1 effectively force individual entries. |

#### Modifiers

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Modifiers (`modifiers`) | [VtItemModifier](units.md#vtitemmodifier)[] | Empty |  | Stat bonuses granted while equipped — same shape as VtBuffDefinition.modifiers. Pushed into VtUnitModifiers under source 'equipment_<slot>' on equip; removed on unequip. |
| Attribute Grants (`attributeGrants`) | [VtAttributeGrant](units.md#vtattributegrant)[] | Empty |  | Primary attribute grants (STR / DEX / INT / VIT / custom) granted while equipped. Pushed into VtUnitModifiers' attribute channel under source 'equipment_<slot>'. |
| Trait Overrides (`traitOverrides`) | [VtTraitOverride](units.md#vttraitoverride)[] | Empty |  | Categorical trait overrides granted while equipped — e.g. armor type Heavy at priority 100, movement type Flying. Pushed into VtUnitTraits under source 'equipment_<slot>'. |

#### Requirements

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Requirements (`requirements`) | [VtItemRequirements](#vtitemrequirements) | — |  | Gates checked at CanEquip / TryEquip time — minimum level, attribute minimums, required unit tag. An empty / default Requirements value means 'no requirements'. |

#### Value

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Value (`value`) | [VtCurrencyAmount](currency.md#vtcurrencyamount) | — |  | Base price. A vendor sells the item at this times its buy multiplier and pays this times its sell multiplier. Leave the currency empty for an item no vendor trades. |

#### Binding & Restrictions

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Is Droppable (`isDroppable`) | `bool` | On |  | If false, the item cannot be removed from a VtUnitInventory through the drop / trade / sell paths (queried via CanDrop / CanTrade / CanSell). Use for quest items, soulbound rewards, hardcoded loadout items. Does NOT block TryRemoveItem (the primitive) or TryUseItem's consume — the library doesn't know which removals are 'drops' vs 'consumes'; only your drop / trade / sell UI does. |
| Is Tradeable (`isTradeable`) | `bool` | On |  | If false, consumer trade UI should refuse to include this item in a trade window. Surfaces as VtUnitInventory.CanTrade. Common pattern: bind-on-pickup MMO loot. |
| Is Sellable (`isSellable`) | `bool` | On |  | If false, consumer vendor UI should refuse to sell this item. Surfaces as VtUnitInventory.CanSell. Common pattern: quest items, set-piece relics. |

#### Consumable / Active Use

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Use Ability (`useAbility`) | [VtAbilityDefinition](abilities.md#vtabilitydefinition) | None |  | Optional ability fired when the item is 'used' from the inventory (potions, scrolls, throwables, charges). Routes through VtUnitAbilities.TryCast so the cast respects cooldowns / GCD / resource cost / interrupts. Self-targeted potions use VtTargetingMode.Self; throwables can use SingleTarget or GroundPoint. Null = item has no active-use behavior (pure stat gear, materials, quest tokens). |
| Consume On Use (`consumeOnUse`) | `bool` | On |  | If true, a successful UseItem call decrements the inventory stack by 1 (charge consumed). Set to false for reusable items like a 'Bandage Kit' that re-charges over time, or a magic scroll that's destroyed only when its inner cooldown expires. |

#### Durability

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Max Durability (`maxDurability`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Maximum durability of one copy. 0 = indestructible (the item ignores ApplyWear calls). Wear is tracked per copy: on the worn slot while worn, on the bag entry while carried, and on the world item while on the ground. |
| Durability Mode (`durabilityMode`) | [VtDurabilityMode](#vtdurabilitymode) | `Condition` |  | Condition: durability is the item's state, capped at Max Durability and restored by repair. Uses: Max Durability is what one copy gives; moving a copy onto another copy of the same item combines them into one with the uses of both, without a limit, and repair does nothing. Uses only combines items that do not stack. |
| Auto Unequip On Break (`autoUnequipOnBreak`) | `bool` | On |  | If true, the item is auto-unequipped when its durability hits 0. If false, the item stays in the slot but its modifiers / grants / overrides remain active — the consumer is then responsible for whatever 'broken item' policy the game wants (greyed icon, stat penalty, etc.). Has no effect when maxDurability is 0. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `bool CombinesDurability { get; }` | True when copies of this item combine their durability: it wears out, its `durabilityMode` is `VtDurabilityMode.Uses` and it does not stack. |
| `bool HasTag(VtItemTagDefinition tag)` | True if this item references the given tag asset. |

## VtItemRarityDefinition

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Items → Item Rarity Definition**.

Designer-authored rarity tier for items — Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, plus any custom tiers a host game adds (Mythic, Artifact, Set, Heirloom, Soulbound, …). Each item references one rarity asset via `VtItemDefinition.rarity`; the rarity drives UI tinting, tooltip styling, sort order in inventories, loot-table weighting, and any consumer-side logic that wants to gate features on tier.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty | Stable string identifier for DB / network payloads. Convention: 'rarity.common', 'rarity.legendary'. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty | UI display name. E.g. 'Common', 'Legendary', 'Mythic'. |
| Description (`description`) | `string` | Empty | Tooltip / lore description. E.g. 'Crafted by master smiths. Uniquely named.' |
| Sort Weight (`sortWeight`) | `int` | 0 | Lower weights sort first in lists / loot tables. Convention: Common 0, Uncommon 100, Rare 200, Epic 300, Legendary 400. Leave gaps for inserts. |
| Color (`color`) | `Color` | `#FFFFFFFF` | Tooltip / inventory text tint for items of this rarity. The shipped rarities use the familiar gray / green / blue / purple / orange palette; change it freely. |
| Icon Background (`iconBackground`) | `Sprite` | None | Optional sprite shown behind the item icon (rarity frame / glow). Null for no background — the consumer's tooltip UI then renders just the tint. |

## VtItemTagDefinition

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Items → Item Tag Definition**.

Designer-authored categorical label for an item — e.g. `Cursed.asset`, `Soulbound.asset`, `Quest.asset`, `VendorTrash.asset`, `Crafted.asset`. Attach to a `VtItemDefinition`.tags array to declare what an item *is*; consumers (loot filters, dismantle UI, trade restrictions, sort views) query via `item.HasTag(tag)`.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty | Stable string identifier for DB / network payloads. Convention: 'tag.cursed', 'tag.soulbound'. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty | UI display name. E.g. 'Cursed', 'Soulbound', 'Quest Item'. |
| Description (`description`) | `string` | Empty | Lore / tooltip description. E.g. 'Cannot be removed once equipped without a Remove Curse spell.' |

## VtItemSetDefinition

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Items → Item Set Definition**.

Designer-authored item set — a collection of items that grants additional bonuses when several members are equipped together. The classic "Warlord's Arsenal: 2 pieces grant +5 Strength; 4 pieces grant +50 Max HP; 6 pieces grant +20% damage" pattern from MMO / ARPG itemization.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty | Stable string identifier — the DB / network payload key. Convention: 'set.warlords_arsenal'. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty | UI display name shown on member tooltips and the set-bonus panel. |
| Description (`description`) | `string` | Empty | Lore / tooltip description shown in the set-bonus panel. |
| Members (`members`) | [VtItemDefinition](#vtitemdefinition)[] | Empty | Member items — the items whose 'set' field references this definition. Used by the editor for validation + tooltip rendering and as a forward index. Runtime counts pieces by walking equipped items, so this list does NOT need to be authoritative for correctness; keeping it in sync is a UX nicety. |
| Tiers (`tiers`) | [VtItemSetTier](#vtitemsettier)[] | Empty | Bonus tiers, sorted ascending by requiredPieces. Each tier independently activates when the wearer has at least requiredPieces members equipped; satisfied tiers stack additively (cumulative model). |

## VtItemRequirements

Serializable struct.

Author-facing gate-bag for an item: level minimum, attribute minimums, optional unit-tag requirement. Inspected by `VtUnitEquipment.CanEquip` before the equip mutation runs.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Level Min (`levelMin`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Minimum unit level required to equip. 0 = no level gate. |
| Attribute Mins (`attributeMins`) | [VtAttributeMinimum](#vtattributeminimum)[] | Empty |  | Attribute minimums (each entry is a (VtAttributeDefinition, minPoints) pair). Resolved against the wearer's current post-modifier attribute totals. Empty = no attribute gate. |
| Required Unit Tag (`requiredUnitTag`) | [VtUnitTagDefinition](units.md#vtunittagdefinition) | None |  | Optional unit-tag gate — the wearer must have this tag to equip. Null = no tag gate. Use cases: 'Paladin-only' weapon (tag.paladin), 'Undead-only' relic (tag.undead). |

## VtItemSetTier

Serializable struct.

One tier of a `VtItemSetDefinition`'s scaling bonuses — e.g. the 2-piece, 4-piece, or 6-piece bonus. Each tier is satisfied independently when the wearer has at least `requiredPieces` set members equipped; satisfied tiers stack additively (cumulative model — the 4pc bonus is layered on top of the 2pc bonus, not a replacement).

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Required Pieces (`requiredPieces`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 1 | Number of equipped set members required to activate this tier. Convention: 2, 4, 6 — but any positive integer is valid. Author tiers in ascending order; the recompute walks them in array order and accepts every tier whose threshold is satisfied. |
| Tooltip Name (`tooltipName`) | `string` | Empty |  | UI label shown in the wearer's set-bonus panel for this tier. E.g. '(2) Set: +5 Strength'. Cosmetic only — the runtime doesn't read this. |
| Modifiers (`modifiers`) | [VtItemModifier](units.md#vtitemmodifier)[] | Empty |  | Stat modifiers granted while this tier is active. Same shape as item modifiers. |
| Attribute Grants (`attributeGrants`) | [VtAttributeGrant](units.md#vtattributegrant)[] | Empty |  | Primary attribute grants (STR / DEX / INT / VIT / custom) granted while this tier is active. |
| Trait Overrides (`traitOverrides`) | [VtTraitOverride](units.md#vttraitoverride)[] | Empty |  | Categorical trait overrides granted while this tier is active. |

## IVtPickable

Interface. Implemented by [VtCraftingStation](crafting.md#vtcraftingstation), [VtQuestGiver](quests.md#vtquestgiver), [VtVendor](vendors.md#vtvendor), [VtWorldItem](#vtworlditem).

Bridge between the input layer and any world-space "thing the player can walk up to and pick up." The shipped `VtWorldItem` implements this for dropped item assets; consumers can implement it on quest-pickup orbs, gold piles, lever-pull interactables, gathered resources, etc., and the `VtTopDownClickInput` right-click flow handles the move-to-then-act chain uniformly.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `Transform Transform { get; }` | The pickable's world-space anchor — the input layer uses this as the move-to target. |
| `float PickupRadius { get; }` | Distance (in world units) within which `TryPickUp` can succeed. The picker walks here, then the input layer fires the pickup when its position is inside this radius. |
| `bool CanBePickedUp { get; }` | Per-pickable gating — false on locked / requires-key / consumed pickables makes the input layer skip them silently. |
| `void TryPickUp(VtUnit picker)` | Run the actual pickup mutation. Implementations should authority- gate via `VtAuthority.IsAuthoritative` if state changes are involved (item moved into a bag, gold added to wallet, quest flag flipped). |

## VtUnitEquipmentVisuals.SlotAttachPoint

Serializable struct.

One row in the slot → attach-point map. Authored on the player prefab inspector; one entry per slot the rig supports. Slots without an entry silently skip visual spawning (e.g. ring slots on a character without finger bones).

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slot (`slot`) | [VtEquipmentSlot](#vtequipmentslot) | `None` | Equipment slot this attach-point serves. Pick the slot the prefab should appear in. |
| Attach Point (`attachPoint`) | `Transform` | None | Transform under which the visual prefab is parented. Typically a bone on the rig (right_hand_socket, head_socket). Required — entries with null transforms are skipped at spawn time. |

## VtAttributeMinimum

Serializable struct.

One "attribute ≥ N" gate used in `VtItemRequirements`. Authors a requirement like "needs 12 Strength to equip" by referencing a `VtAttributeDefinition` asset and a minimum point total.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Attribute (`attribute`) | [VtAttributeDefinition](units.md#vtattributedefinition) | None |  | Which primary attribute the wearer must possess at least minPoints of. Pick from the dropdown of every VtAttributeDefinition asset in the project. |
| Min Points (`minPoints`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Minimum point total required (resolved post-modifier total — base + items + buffs). |

## Enums

### VtTwoHandRule

What `VtUnitEquipment` does with the off-hand item when a two-handed item goes into the main hand. Serialized as int; append only.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `OffHandComesOff` | The off-hand item comes off into the bag. Putting an item in the off hand is refused while a two-hander is held. |
| `OffHandSuspended` | The off-hand item stays worn but gives nothing while the two-hander is held, and counts again when it leaves. A torch or shield comes back when you switch away from a bow. |
| `OffHandBlocksTwoHander` | A two-handed item cannot go on while an off-hand item is worn; take the off-hand item off first. |

### VtEquipmentSlot

The set of equipment slots an item can occupy on a unit. Used as the key for the slot map on `VtUnitEquipment` and as the source-id suffix when equipped items push their modifiers / attributes / traits (`"equipment_<slot>"`).

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `None` | Inventory-only / non-equippable. Potions, materials, quest items. |
| `Head` | Helm / hat / hood. |
| `Chest` | Chestpiece / robe / breastplate. |
| `Legs` | Leg armor / pants / greaves. |
| `Feet` | Boots / sandals / sabatons. |
| `Hands` | Gloves / gauntlets / bracers. |
| `MainHand` | Primary weapon. 2H weapons occupy this slot and block `OffHand`. |
| `OffHand` | Off-hand weapon, shield, or focus. Auto-unequipped when a 2H is equipped to `MainHand`. |
| `Neck` | Necklace / amulet / pendant. |
| `Ring1` | First ring slot. Members of the Ring family. |
| `Ring2` | Second ring slot. Members of the Ring family. |
| `Trinket1` | First trinket slot. Members of the Trinket family. |
| `Trinket2` | Second trinket slot. Members of the Trinket family. |
| `Back` | Worn on the back: backpack, cloak, quiver. |

### VtEquipFailureReason

Why an attempted `VtUnitEquipment.TryEquip` / `VtUnitEquipment.CanEquip` call refused the operation. Returned via the `out` parameter so callers (UI tooltips, AI, item-pickup handlers) can surface a precise reason without guesswork.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `None` | The operation succeeded — the request would equip cleanly. |
| `NullItem` | The supplied item was null. |
| `SlotMismatch` | The slot the caller asked for doesn't match the item's authored slot (and isn't in the same family for ring / trinket items). |
| `LevelTooLow` | The wearer's level is below the item's `VtItemRequirements.levelMin`. |
| `AttributeTooLow` | The wearer's resolved attribute totals don't satisfy one of `VtItemRequirements.attributeMins`. |
| `MissingRequiredTag` | The wearer doesn't have `VtItemRequirements.requiredUnitTag`. |
| `SlotOccupiedBlocked` | A slot conflict that cannot be auto-resolved — typically equipping into `VtEquipmentSlot.OffHand` while a two-handed weapon occupies `VtEquipmentSlot.MainHand`. Caller must unequip the conflicting slot first. |
| `AuthorityNotLocal` | The caller is not the authoritative owner of this unit. In multiplayer modes `VtUnitEquipment.TryEquip` rejects on replicas; the authoritative side mutates and the net layer mirrors via `VtUnitEquipment.ApplyEquippedFromNet`. |
| `NotInInventory` | `VtUnitEquipment.TryEquipFromInventory` was asked for an item the unit's bag does not hold. |
| `InventoryFull` | The unit's bag has no room for the item taken off. |
| `WouldOverflowInventory` | The item adds to the bag's capacity, and without it the bag could no longer hold what it holds. Empty the bag first. |
| `TargetSlotRefused` | The bag slot named to take the item holds something that cannot be worn there, is shut, or its rules refuse the item. |
| `HeldSlotFull` | A `VtUnitHeldSlot` holds the main hand and its area has no free slot for the item. |

### VtDurabilityMode

How an item's durability behaves, set on `VtItemDefinition.durabilityMode`. Only matters for items with a `VtItemDefinition.maxDurability` above 0. Serialized as int; append only.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Condition` | Durability is the item's condition: it wears down to 0, never goes above `VtItemDefinition.maxDurability`, and repair restores it. Copies never combine. |
| `Uses` | Durability is a number of uses: `VtItemDefinition.maxDurability` is what one copy gives. Moving a copy onto another copy of the same item combines them into one with the uses of both, without a limit. Repair does nothing. Only items that do not stack combine. |
